note: Tone-shift labels for the §11 'FOMC tone' eval, re-derived on 2026-09-26 from the REAL statement text (saved in evals/macro/fixtures/fomc/, extracted from federalreserve.gov) and the code-computed sentence diff, not from memory. They remain PROVISIONAL until a human confirms them: tone is a judgment call, and pairs marked confidence 'low' are genuinely arguable. Two labels changed from the previous session's memory-based proposal (2023-12-13->2024-01-31 and 2024-06-12->2024-07-31, see `changed_from`); the ambiguous 2024-09-18->2024-11-07 pair was dropped and the 2026 hike and near-identical pairs added. Coverage per §11: a cut, a hike (two), holds with notable language changes (two), and a near-identical pair that must be 'unchanged'.

pairs.label: more_dovish
pairs.reasoning: First cut of the cycle and a 50 bp one. Edits: 'Job gains have moderated' -> 'have slowed' [1]; adds 'gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent' [5]; removes the 'does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range' guardrail [9]; the commitment now reads 'supporting maximum employment and returning inflation' [11].

pairs.label: more_hawkish
pairs.reasoning: 50 bp hike after 25 bp. Adds 'The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks.' [8]; balance-sheet language moves from 'expects to begin reducing' to 'decided to begin reducing ... on June 1' [12]; inflation-pressure language firmed from 'likely to create' to 'are creating additional upward pressure on inflation' [5].

pairs.label: more_hawkish
pairs.reasoning: 25 bp hike after a 9-3 hold where three members preferred a hike. Decision sentence changes from maintain to raise [0]; adds 'Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.' [9]; inflation described bluntly as 'Inflation remains elevated.' [8].

pairs.label: more_dovish
pairs.reasoning: Hold, but every edit softens: 'Job gains have remained strong' -> 'have moderated, and the unemployment rate has moved up' [1]; inflation 'remains elevated' -> 'remains somewhat elevated' [2]; 'modest' -> 'some further progress' [3]; 'remains highly attentive to inflation risks' -> 'attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate' [6].
pairs.changed_from: unchanged (memory-based guess that these were near-identical; the real diff has 5 dovish edits)

pairs.label: more_dovish
pairs.reasoning: Hold. Drops the tightening bias ('In determining the extent of any additional policy firming...' [10]) and the credit-conditions paragraph [3-5]; adds 'risks ... are moving into better balance' [11] and frames the next move as 'adjustments to the target range' [13]. Against that it adds 'does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence' [14], a hawkish guardrail on cuts that the December text never discussed. Net textual shift judged dovish (from a hiking bias to a cutting discussion); the market read at the time was hawkish relative to expectations, which is why this pair is arguable.
pairs.changed_from: more_hawkish (memory-based, relative to the market's read of December rather than to the December text)

pairs.label: unchanged
pairs.reasoning: Near-identical pair: the only edit is 'The Committee reaffirmed its policy of maintaining ample reserves' -> 'The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves' [1]. (The 9-3 vote with three members preferring a hike is not statement language.) §11 requires this pair to be 'unchanged'.
